words.gram: genitive singular, feminine (with negative не будет)

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?
Did something happen?
What kind of nonsense is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of nonsense is this?
This is a service for our guests.
This does not interrupt your rest.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: And what should I do?
And I do not want to be anyone else.
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: And right now excuse me.
Sorry, I thought the wrong thing.
What was that? Excuse me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'eyes' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Open your eyes.
Alright, I agree to that.
And where is your top management?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.trans: The grand opening is tomorrow.
Understand, Vitya, the opening is tomorrow.

examples.text: Я проверяю, всё ли готово к открытию.
examples.trans: I am checking whether everything is ready for the opening.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Sorry, I did it by accident.
Are you by any chance Samson?
I met him by chance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: I am listening to you.
Listen, tell me right now.
Listen, I actually came to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
My butterfly.
The baby is only five months along.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You should introduce a new service.
You are simply spying on me.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'arrived', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.
I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
And start!
Today we have a draw.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the very').

examples.trans: I came here for a real reason.
Fine, I will go up myself right now.
You yourselves asked for five kilograms.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'practice, deed' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I came here for a real reason.
Please make coffee for the tables.
What are you doing in there right now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.
Do you know Katya?
In short, he knows what it is for.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'whom', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!
Victoria Sergeevna, people came to see you.
Victor Petrovich, there is a new order here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
And right now excuse me.
Listen, tell me right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'called', paired with 'называть'.

examples.trans: Who did you just name?
You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.
examples.trans: A new service operates in our hotel.
This is a service for our guests.
Do not disturb our rest.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
I am with you.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!
There are cockroaches in your kitchen.

examples.text: Быстро уберите всех тараканов с кухни!
examples.trans: Quickly remove all the cockroaches from the kitchen!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'boyfriend / guy' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ей нравится, когда ей доверяет парень.
examples.trans: She likes it when her boyfriend trusts her.

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.
I am her boyfriend, got it?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I have no idea.
I am her boyfriend, got it?
What? I did not understand you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
I have no idea.
No, nothing.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: A restroom must be earned first.
You should not hit on her.
We need to give the money to Timur.

meanings.en: to pester, to bother, to harass (+ к + dat.)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ставать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hit on / pester', paired with 'пристать'.

examples.trans: You should not hit on her.
They were pestering Nina.

examples.text: Не приставай ко мне с вопросами!
examples.trans: Stop pestering me with questions!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: What are you talking about at all?
Who are you at all?
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: Do not even dare to say that.
What are you talking about at all?

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hang in there'.

related.gloss: not to hang in there (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?
I need to stay further away from her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'альше').

examples.trans: Stay far away from my girlfriend!
Stand a little further back behind the pines.
Step a little further away from the fire.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The grand opening is tomorrow.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.

examples.text: Вы сможете посмотреть на работу шефа.
examples.trans: You will be able to watch the chef's work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh my God.

examples.text: Ну что, Витя, теперь ты мой раб.
examples.trans: Well then, Vitya, now you are my servant.
At least give my office back.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a girl' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Stay far away from my girlfriend!

examples.text: Девушки, как я, у тебя не будет!
examples.trans: You'll never have a girl like me!
This is my girlfriend Lyolya.
